text: I feel more energized after spending time with a group than after time alone.
I process my thoughts best by talking them through out loud with other people.
I enjoy striking up conversations with strangers while waiting in line or at events.
I need real alone time to recharge after socializing, even with people I enjoy.
I'd rather draft my thoughts privately before sharing them than think out loud in a group.
A quiet evening with one close friend appeals to me far more than a big party.
I trust what I can directly observe or experience over abstract theory.
I'm more interested in the practical details of a plan than its big-picture concept.
I'd rather follow a proven method than improvise my own approach to a task.
I'm drawn to abstract ideas and future possibilities more than present, concrete facts.
I regularly find myself imagining how things could be, rather than focusing on how they are.
I enjoy spotting patterns that connect ideas from completely different fields.
When making a decision, I weigh logic and consistency above how it will make people feel.
I'd rather give someone an honest, critical assessment than a comforting but vague one.
I evaluate arguments on their merits, not on who is making them or how they're delivered.
When making a decision, how it affects the people involved matters more to me than strict logic.
I naturally consider people's feelings before I consider being right.
I find it hard to stay detached when someone I care about is upset.
I like to have things decided and settled well ahead of time.
I keep a to-do list or schedule and feel uneasy when I fall behind on it.
I prefer closing out one task fully before starting another.
I like to keep my options open rather than lock in a plan too early.
I work best under a looming deadline rather than a steady early schedule.
I enjoy jumping between several projects at once rather than finishing one before starting the next.
I tend to take the lead and speak up first in group settings.
I can go a full day without talking to anyone and not feel bothered by it.
I actively seek out art, music, or ideas that are unconventional or experimental.
I enjoy questioning my own long-held beliefs when presented with a good counter-argument.
I prefer familiar routines and tested approaches over novel, untested ones.
I keep my living or work space organized without having to force myself.
I follow through on commitments even when my initial motivation has faded.
I often start tasks with good intentions but lose steam before finishing them.
I double-check my work carefully before considering it done.
I go out of my way to avoid inconveniencing other people.
I generally assume people have good intentions unless proven otherwise.
I find it satisfying to win an argument, even at the cost of the other person's feelings.
I forgive people relatively quickly, even after a real conflict.
I'd rather negotiate hard for my own interests than compromise for the sake of harmony.
I find myself replaying embarrassing moments long after they happened.
Small setbacks can put me in a bad mood for the rest of the day.
I generally stay calm and level-headed, even when things go wrong.
I worry about things going badly even when there's no clear evidence they will.
My mood tends to be steady and doesn't swing much from day to day.
I feel anxious in situations where I don't know what's expected of me.
I hold myself to a strict internal standard of what's right, and I feel guilty when I fall short of it.
I notice flaws and inefficiencies that others overlook, and I feel compelled to correct them.
I feel most valuable when I'm taking care of other people's needs.
I have a hard time asking for help, even though I'm quick to offer it to others.
I adjust how I present myself depending on what will earn approval or admiration.
Being seen as successful matters to me more than most people would guess.
I feel like there's something fundamentally different about me compared to most people.
I'm drawn to depth and emotional intensity, and ordinary small talk feels hollow to me.
I'd rather understand something thoroughly on my own than rely on others to explain it.
I protect my time and energy carefully, and I resent demands that feel intrusive.
I tend to anticipate what could go wrong before I commit to something.
I value loyalty and consistency in relationships, and I test whether people will really show up.
I keep my options and plans open because I hate the idea of missing out on something better.
I distract myself with new activities or ideas rather than sit with uncomfortable feelings.
I speak my mind directly and don't back down easily once I've taken a position.
I have a strong instinct to protect people I care about, even if it means confrontation.
I go along with what others want in order to keep the peace, even when I have a preference.
It's hard for me to identify what I actually want when other people's preferences are in the room.
I take what people say literally and often miss sarcasm or implied meaning.
People have told me my tone of voice doesn't always match what I'm feeling or saying.
I find myself talking at length about a topic without noticing whether the other person is still interested.
I sometimes use words or phrases in a way that others find unusual or overly formal.
I find it genuinely hard to know what response is expected of me in a social situation.
I have to consciously work out social rules that seem to come naturally to other people.
I struggle to tell when someone wants to end a conversation.
Making eye contact during conversation feels uncomfortable or effortful to me.
I've been told I come across as blunt or insensitive, even when I didn't mean to.
Certain sounds, lights, or textures are distracting or uncomfortable to me in a way that doesn't seem to bother other people.
I'm often described as clumsy or physically awkward.
I engage in repetitive movements, like tapping, rocking, or pacing, when I'm stressed or concentrating.
Crowded, loud environments quickly become overwhelming for me.
I don't always notice hunger, pain, or tiredness until it becomes hard to ignore.
I have one or two topics I could talk about in great depth for hours.
I get so absorbed in something I'm interested in that I lose track of time or forget to eat.
Unexpected changes to my plans or routine are more distressing to me than they seem to be for others.
I collect detailed knowledge about specific subjects, well beyond what's practically useful.
